Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r=7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{(7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{49{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +49{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{49}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}7\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =7\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =7(\frac{\pi }{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
